Subject: Re: Model fit + tool-calling evals — next steps

Thanks again for your time today, Judy — really helpful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: reliable structured extraction from customer support transcripts (JSON schema output) + occasional tool/function calls to pull KB context.
- Success criteria you gave: >= 95% JSON schema compliance on production prompt set, <2% critical hallucinations, end-to-end 95th pctl latency < 350ms for short responses.

What we did / recommend next: 
1) Model candidates (initial eval): 
   - rw-infer-13b-quant (cost-efficient, good structured output with schema-guided decoding)
   - rw-infer-70b-fp16 (higher quality on long-context extractions; higher cost)

2) Eval artifacts attached: prompt set (avery-prompt-set-v1.json) and a short eval summary (eval-summary-20270810.pdf). The prompt set contains 250 representative transcripts and the target JSON schema.

3) Tool/function calling notes: 
   - We validated function call formatting in a sandbox; main failure mode we saw was partial JSON (trailing tokens) in ~4% of cases for the 13b quant baseline.
   - Mitigations: iterative schema validation with server-side retries (up to 2 auto-retries with temperature anneal + forced JSON mode), and a lightweight repair pass using a deterministic parser to fix trailing commas/unfinished tokens.

4) Proposed next steps: 
   - Redwood runs a short (2-day) focused eval on your prompt set across both candidate models with our structured-output harness.
   - We'll share detailed per-field precision/recall, schema compliance rates, and a reproducible notebook.
   - Follow-up call to review results and choose bench model + rollout plan (canary % and autoscale settings).

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min review on Wed 8/12 or Thu 8/13? Also let us know if you want us to include latency profiling under your expected concurrency (we can run a small throughput test).

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Judy Park <judy@averyanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-11T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit + tool-calling evals — next steps (technical details)

Hi Judy — happy to dig into the failure modes. Short answers up-front, details below.
\Summary: The ~4% failure for rw-infer-13b-quant breaks down roughly as: 
- 2.1% truncated / early-termination (model stops before finishing JSON)
- 1.2% type mismatches (e.g., numeric fields returned as strings)
- 0.7% missing required keys
\Root causes and mitigations we plan to run in the focused eval: 
1) Truncation: often due to tokenization + temperature causing early stop. Mitigation: forced JSON mode (we bias tokens toward closing braces) + autoregressive retry with max_tokens increased on retry. In our tests, a single retry with deterministic closing bias fixes ~70% of truncations.
\2) Type mismatches: we apply a schema-aware post-processor that coerces numeric-like strings to numbers and validates enums; we log each coercion for audit. For fields where coercion is ambiguous we surface to the repair queue.
\3) Missing keys: for certain optional fields this is expected; for required keys we run a deterministic filler that either backfills from context or flags the record for manual review. Our target for the eval is to bring required-key omissions below 0.5%.
\Retries and quotas: retries do count as requests in the hosted usage model. For Dedicated we can configure server-side retries that do not count against a customer's per-token quota (they remain internal retry attempts on Redwood's side) — we can include an option in the Dedicated proposal.
\Latency/SLA guidance (Dedicated): 
- rw-infer-13b-quant (dedicated pool, optimized kernels): expected P95 ~ 140–220ms, P99 ~ 280–420ms for short responses (under 200 tokens) at moderate concurrency.
- rw-infer-70b-fp16 (dedicated high-memory): expected P95 ~ 220–350ms, P99 ~ 420–650ms.
\We'll include example manifests of the repair flow and a small Jupyter notebook demonstrating the parser + one real failing transcript when we deliver the eval artifacts.
— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Model fit + tool-calling evals — next steps (model notes)

Judy — quick notes on model tradeoffs and what we'll include in the eval: 

- 13b-quant: great cost profile, compresses well with our quantization pipeline. Expect slightly higher type/coherence errors on noisy transcripts. Good candidate for canary/working set where throughput/cost matters.
- 70b-fp16: strong at consistency, better at long-context extraction and nested JSON. Higher cost but fewer post-processing repairs.
\Benchmark plan for the 2-day eval: 
- Per-field precision/recall, schema compliance, token-level latency distribution, and retry rate.
- We'll run both models across your 250-example prompt set at 1–5 rps to measure realistic latency under light concurrency.
- We'll provide a recommended rollout: start with 13b-quant for 10% of traffic + repair pipeline, then shift to 70b for high-confidence routes if the cost delta is acceptable.
\Link to the raw benchmark notebook: https://drive.redwood.com/avery/fit-evals/20270810 (will drop the notebook there).
— Aditya
Applied ML — Redwood Inference
